paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: : The performance on BioGPT.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the accuracy percentage for six different methods evaluated across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and utilizes a logarithmic scale with major tick marks visibly labeled at 0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)", employing a linear scale with values ranging from below 30 to roughly 60, featuring tick labels at intervals of 5 units from 30 to 55. Data points for all lines are positioned at approximate x-axis values of 3, 30, 300, and 3000. The "Base" method is represented by a solid black line with circular markers; it begins at a y-value of approximately 28.5, rises to 30.8 at x=30, increases slightly to 32.2 at x=300, and remains steady, ending at 32.2 at x=3000. The "FT" method is shown as a solid blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, starting at 31.9, rising to 35.8 at x=30, continuing to 37.2 at x=300, and concluding at 38.3. The "IKE" method is depicted by a solid red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, starting at 32.5, increasing to 37.6 at x=30, reaching 39.5 at x=300, and ending at 41.4. The "MEND" method is represented by a solid brown line with diamond markers, commencing at 36.4, moving up to 40.8 at x=30, climbing to 44.8 at x=300, and finishing with a slight increase to 45.4. The "MEMIT" method is a solid purple line with hexagonal markers, initiating at 35.9, experiencing an increase to 43.1 at x=30, rising to 45.7 at x=300, and ending at 46.5. Finally, the "ROME" method is plotted as a solid green line with square markers, starting at 43.7, increasing to 49.2 at x=30, rising to 56.1 at x=300, and reaching a final high value of 58.8 at x=3000.
